The arch form can be influenced by both the sagittal molar relationship and the Bolton tooth-size discrepancy. 

1. **Sagittal Molar Relationship**: The sagittal molar relationship, which refers to the anteroposterior (front-to-back) relationship of the upper and lower molars, can affect the arch form. For instance, a Class II or Class III molar relationship may require adjustments in the arch form to achieve proper occlusion and aesthetics.

2. **Bolton Tooth-Size Discrepancy**: The Bolton tooth-size discrepancy refers to the difference in the overall size of the upper and lower teeth. A significant discrepancy can influence the arch form, as it may necessitate compensatory adjustments to ensure proper fit and alignment of the teeth within the dental arch.

In summary, both factors can influence the arch form, but the extent of their influence can vary depending on the individual case and the specific orthodontic or orthopedic treatment goals.
